results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801) are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system (vfb). According to the VFB database, the mushroom body is divided into these three parts: the calyx, which receives sensory interneuron afferents; the pedunculus, a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes; and the mushroom body lobe system, consisting of a vertical branch and a medial branch, which have different structures at different life stages (vfb).

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: According to the VFB database ("vfb"), there are several types of [Kenyon cells](http://virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247) in the adult Drosophila brain. These include alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which can be further subdivided into subtypes such as core, surface, posterior, anterior-posterior, middle, dorsal, and others ("vfb"). Additionally, gamma Kenyon cells have subclasses including KCg-s1, KCg-s2, KCg-s3, and KCg-s4 ("vfb").

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response:
The [LPLC2](FBbt_00111763) visual neuron type is a lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron with a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer (vfb). Its cell body lies in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind (vfb, citing Wu et al., 2016). 

The [LPLC2](FBbt_00111763) neuron detects looming (expansion) stimuli (vfb, citing Klapoetke et al., 2017). Its activity elicits a jump escape response (vfb). 

The [LPLC2](FBbt_00111763) neuron is connected to various neuron classes, including adult VPNd1 lineage neurons, adult cholinergic neurons, and other lobula plate-lobula columnar neurons (vfb). Additionally, it has connections to T5c neurons and transmedullary neurons (vfb). 

Note: The specific details of the connections and the function of the [LPLC2](FBbt_00111763) neuron are based on the information available in the vfb database, which in turn cites literature sources such as Wu et al., 2016, and Klapoetke et al., 2017. However, the full citations for these literature sources are not provided in the given evidence.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The giant fiber neuron ([FBbt_00004020](http://virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020)) is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior (source: "vfb" [Thomas and Wyman, 1984]). 

Anatomically, the giant fiber neuron has a large descending axon and arborizes in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center (source: "vfb"). There is one of these cells per hemisphere (source: "vfb" [Koto et al., 1981; Namiki et al., 2018; Sturner et al., 2025]) and its large cell body is located posterior to the lower protocerebrum (source: "vfb" [Koto et al., 1981]). 

Several driver lines are available for the giant fiber neuron, including GMR91H05-GAL4, GMR79D08-GAL4, and GMR78G07-GAL4 (source: "vfb"). 

Relevant publications on the giant fiber neuron include Lee and Godenschwege, 2015, and Vaughan et al., 2014 (source: "vfb"), as well as Kamikouchi et al., 2009 (source: "vfb" [Kamikouchi et al., 2009]). 

the provided evidence does not contain detailed information on the connectivity of the giant fiber neuron beyond its arborization in the antennal mechanosensory and motor center. For a comprehensive understanding of its connectivity, further research or consultation of additional sources may be necessary.
